parsed.explanation: The quoted sentence appears verbatim in the "Current best" section and, in context, is the write-up's own admission that the finiteness claim (only finitely many primes ever impose new restrictions — obligation (F)) still needs a rigorous proof. Scanning the whole text: the "Approaches tried" section only records computational data (a1=15, 35, prime powers) and states a "Conjecture"; the "Full proof" section reads "(Not yet complete.)". No argument for all terms is given anywhere, and even the ensuing sentence notes the natural formulation is "circular because A depends on the sequence". Since the large-prime-erasure/finiteness lemma is the crux on which L = product of finitely many primes and the periodicity assembly depend, its absence leaves the proof invalid as written.
